# `supersql` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha`.

## Package documentation

Package supersql is an embedded, single-process database that speaks a
conformant subset of PostgreSQL 18 SQL. A host opens a Catalog with Open (or
a database/sql Connector with OpenConnector, or a pgx/v5-compatible pool via
github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/pgx) and supplies a certified clock such as
github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/clock/local; there is no server, no network
listener, and no DSN.

OpenOptions.Clock is required and borrowed: the host owns the clock
provider's lifecycle and must close the database before closing it. Storage
layout, the SQL surface, and the conformance position are generated under
docs/reference by internal/tools/docgen.

### `func RestorePITR(ctx context.Context, baseBackupDir string, walArchiveDir string, targetTS clock.Instant, options PITRRestoreOptions) (*Catalog, PITRResult, error)`

RestorePITR restores baseBackupDir into options.Open.Directory, replays every
contiguous archived WAL segment from walArchiveDir with commitTS <= targetTS,
and opens the recovered database strictly at or before targetTS.

RestorePITRFromChain restores an incremental backup chain into
options.Open.Directory, replays contiguous archived WAL segments from
walArchiveDir with commitTS <= targetTS, and opens the recovered database.

SQLState returns the PostgreSQL SQLSTATE carried by an error produced by the

### `type Catalog`

Catalog is one opened native database. It owns the backend, workers,
transaction manager and session services, and borrows the host clock.


```go
// Catalog is one opened native database. It owns the backend, workers,
// transaction manager and session services, and borrows the host clock.

```

#### `func Open(ctx context.Context, options OpenOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

Open composes the native session stack over Directory and returns the owning
database: backend, transaction manager, control-plane stores and session
services. A fresh directory is bootstrapped in one atomic catalog statement; a
bootstrapped database is reopened from its durable manifest. The host-supplied
clock is borrowed, never replaced. Open never reads wall time, keeps no
package-level registry, and never constructs a clock of its own.


#### `func RestoreCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, backupDir string, options OpenOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

RestoreCheckpoint restores the backup at backupDir into options.Directory —
which must be missing or empty — verifies every manifest file and the
persisted certified fence, then opens the restored database under Open's
readiness rules: writable restoration certifies a fresh fence above the
restored frontier, while HistoricalReadOnly serves retained snapshots without
a synchronized clock.


#### `func RestoreEncryptedCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, backupDir string, encryptionKey []byte, options OpenOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

RestoreEncryptedCheckpoint restores an encrypted (or unencrypted) full
checkpoint backup from backupDir into options.Directory, verifies the
encryption key fingerprint, file checksums, and certified read fence, then
opens the restored database under Open's readiness rules.


#### `func RestoreIncremental(ctx context.Context, chainDirs []string, options IncrementalRestoreOptions) (*Catalog, error)`

RestoreIncremental validates a full-plus-incremental backup chain
[baseDir, inc1Dir, ...], verifies parent lineage, decryption keys, checksums,
and certified read fence, reconstructs the database at options.Open.Directory,
and opens it.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Close() error`

Close releases the session, allocator, transaction manager, backend and
workers. It is safe to call repeatedly and reports the first error while still
releasing every owned collaborator.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CopyFrom(ctx context.Context, statement string, source io.Reader, options CopyOptions) (CopyResult, error)`

CopyFrom executes one COPY ... FROM STDIN statement, reading records from
source until EOF. The caller keeps ownership of source; the engine never
closes it. Server-side COPY FROM 'file' and FROM PROGRAM are excluded
features and fail with SQLSTATE 0A000.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CopyTo(ctx context.Context, statement string, sink io.Writer, options CopyOptions) (CopyResult, error)`

CopyTo executes one COPY ... TO STDOUT statement, writing records to sink.
The caller keeps ownership of sink; the engine never closes it. Server-side
COPY TO 'file' and TO PROGRAM are excluded features and fail with SQLSTATE
0A000.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CreateHotBackup(ctx context.Context, targetDir string) error`

CreateHotBackup captures one certified closed snapshot — the backend file
set plus the fence secret — into targetDir, which must be missing or empty.
The backup is immutable and internally checksummed; RestoreCheckpoint opens
it at a destination. Historical-only databases re-publish their persisted
closed frontier.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CreateHotBackupWithOptions(ctx context.Context, targetDir string, options BackupOptions) error`

CreateHotBackupWithOptions captures one certified closed snapshot into
targetDir, optionally encrypting every backed-up file with AES-256-GCM when
options.EncryptionKey is provided.


#### `func (database *Catalog) CreateIncrementalBackup(ctx context.Context, baseBackupDir string, options IncrementalBackupOptions) (IncrementalBackupInfo, error)`

CreateIncrementalBackup captures one certified closed snapshot relative to
baseBackupDir (a full backup or an earlier incremental backup) into
options.Destination, copying only newly created or modified files and
recording unchanged files as inherited references.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Directory() string`

Directory reports the database directory this instance was opened on.


#### `func (database *Catalog) EnableWALArchive(ctx context.Context, archiveDir string, encryptionKey []byte) error`

EnableWALArchive enables atomic WAL segment archiving on an open database.
Every existing unretired WAL segment and every subsequent durable commit WAL
segment is atomically copied to archiveDir (encrypted with AES-256-GCM when
encryptionKey is non-empty) before WAL retirement can unlink it.


#### `func (database *Catalog) MaintenanceError() error`

MaintenanceError reports the most recent background maintenance failure, or
nil when every pass since Open succeeded. The loop exits on a fatal failure
and delivers it to Close; a long-running host observes the same error here
without closing the database.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Metrics(ctx context.Context) DatabaseMetrics`

Metrics returns a live snapshot of query, auto-ANALYZE, storage backlog, and
block-cache counters for the database.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Notify(channel, payload string) error`

Notify publishes a notification directly to all listeners on channel.
It validates PostgreSQL channel (<= 63 bytes, non-empty) and payload
(<= 8000 bytes) limits.


#### `func (database *Catalog) RegisterTextSearchAnalyzer(name string, analyzer TextSearchAnalyzer) error`

RegisterTextSearchAnalyzer registers or replaces a custom Go text search
configuration under name on this database. Configuration names follow
PostgreSQL identifier rules (ASCII case-folded to lowercase, non-empty,
at most 63 bytes, valid UTF-8, without NUL bytes or dots).

Registration is safe for concurrent use alongside active SQL queries.


#### `func (database *Catalog) RunAutoAnalyze(ctx context.Context) (int, error)`

RunAutoAnalyze executes ANALYZE on every table whose accumulated mutations
have reached the configured auto-ANALYZE threshold, resetting each analyzed
table's pending mutation counter. It returns the number of tables analyzed.


#### `func (database *Catalog) Subscribe(channels ...string) *Subscription`

Subscribe registers an in-process Go listener on one or more PostgreSQL
LISTEN/NOTIFY channels. Channel names are normalized case-insensitively like
unquoted SQL identifiers.


#### `func (database *Catalog) UnregisterTextSearchAnalyzer(name string)`

UnregisterTextSearchAnalyzer removes a previously registered custom text
search configuration by name. Unregistering an unknown name is a no-op.

Unregistration is safe for concurrent use alongside active SQL queries.

### `type Connector`

Connector is a driver.Connector that owns one opened Catalog. Every Connect
creates a connection with its own session, so settings, prepared statements,
cursors, advisory locks, temporary relations and active transactions never
cross connections. The host owns close order: sql.DB first, then the
Connector, then the clock provider. Close releases the database, so no live
connection may outlive it.

```go
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

#### `func NewConnectorWithCatalog(database *Catalog) *Connector`

NewConnectorWithCatalog returns a Connector bound to an already opened
Catalog. Close on the returned Connector closes the underlying Catalog.


#### `func OpenConnector(ctx context.Context, options OpenOptions) (*Connector, error)`

OpenConnector opens the native database like Open and returns the connector
that serves driver.Conn sessions over it.


##### Example: `OpenConnector`

ExampleOpenConnector runs the README quick start verbatim: OpenConnector uses
localclock.New(), sql.OpenDB adapts it, and the printed account proves the
committed rows read back.


```go
ctx := context.Background()
dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "supersql-example-*")
if err != nil {
	panic(err)
}
defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
if err := runReadme(ctx, dir, os.Stdout); err != nil {
	panic(err)
}
// Output:
Account: 1 | Alice | 50000
```

#### `func (connector *Connector) Catalog() *Catalog`

Catalog returns the underlying Catalog owned by this connector.


#### `func (connector *Connector) Close() error`

Close releases the owning Catalog. The host must have closed its sql.DB
first so no live connection outlives the database.


#### `func (connector *Connector) Connect(ctx context.Context) (driver.Conn, error)`

Connect returns a driver.Conn bound to a new isolated sessionScope. It fails
with ErrDatabaseClosed after Close or once the owning Catalog is closed.


#### `func (connector *Connector) Driver() driver.Driver`

Driver returns the shared Driver value that produced this connector.

### `type Driver`

Driver cannot construct a connection by itself: a certified clock is not
expressible in a DSN, and no global provider lookup exists. Connections come
only from OpenConnector, which owns the clock's Catalog.


```go

// expressible in a DSN, and no global provider lookup exists. Connections come
// only from OpenConnector, which owns the clock's Catalog.
type Driver struct{}
```

#### `func (Driver) Open(string) (driver.Conn, error)`

Open always fails with ErrClockRequired: a certified clock is not expressible
in a DSN. Use OpenConnector.


#### `func (Driver) OpenConnector(string) (driver.Connector, error)`

OpenConnector always fails with ErrClockRequired. Use OpenConnector.

### `type OpenOptions`

OpenOptions configures Open. Clock is required and borrowed: the host owns
provider startup and shutdown and must close the database before closing the
provider, because a live database holds fences certified by that provider.


```go
// OpenOptions configures Open. Clock is required and borrowed: the host owns
// provider startup and shutdown and must close the database before closing the
// provider, because a live database holds fences certified by that provider.
type OpenOptions struct {
	// Directory is the database directory. Open creates it when absent.
	Directory	string
	// Compaction overrides individual storage backend resource limits when
	// nonzero; zero fields inherit DefaultCompactionConfig().
	Compaction	CompactionConfig
	// Clock is the certified time source borrowed by the database.
	Clock	clock.Clock
	// Maintenance bounds the background reclamation loop Open starts. The zero
	// value selects the defaults; Maintenance.Disabled stops the loop.
	Maintenance	MaintenanceConfig
	// HistoryRetention configures the durable MVCC history retention window.
	// Zero selects the default (24h); negative values are rejected by Open.
	HistoryRetention	time.Duration
	// HistoricalReadOnly opens the database without requiring fresh certified
	// readiness: no writes and no latest reads are accepted, only retained
	// historical snapshots are served. The clock may be unsynchronized.
	HistoricalReadOnly	bool
	// Parallelism sets the execution worker pool concurrency. Zero or negative
	// selects runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0).
	Parallelism	int
	// MemoryBudgetBytes overrides the shared query memory budget (default 256 MiB).
	MemoryBudgetBytes	uint64
	// TransactionMemoryBytes overrides the per-transaction in-memory staging limit (default 8 MiB).
	TransactionMemoryBytes	uint64
	// TransactionSpillBytes overrides the per-transaction spill limit (default 32 MiB).
	TransactionSpillBytes	uint64
	// MaxTransactions overrides the maximum concurrent active transactions (default 64).
	MaxTransactions	int
	// MaxOperations overrides the maximum concurrent snapshot/read operations (default 64).
	MaxOperations	int
	// Observer receives one QueryEvent after each completed SQL statement.
	// Nil disables per-query observer notifications.
	Observer	QueryObserver
	// SlowQueryThreshold marks statements whose duration meets or exceeds this
	// value as slow queries. Zero disables slow-query tracking; negative values
	// are rejected by Open.
	SlowQueryThreshold	time.Duration
	// OnSlowQuery is invoked when a statement's duration meets or exceeds
	// SlowQueryThreshold. Nil disables the callback while still incrementing
	// DatabaseMetrics.SlowQueriesTotal when SlowQueryThreshold > 0.
	OnSlowQuery	func(context.Context, QueryEvent)
	// EncryptionKey enables optional pure-Go AES-256-GCM at-rest encryption for
	// newly written SST runs, WAL files, and encrypted backups when set to a
	// 32-byte key. Nil disables at-rest encryption.
	EncryptionKey	[]byte
	// WALArchiveDir enables continuous WAL segment archiving into the given
	// directory for Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR). Empty disables WAL archiving.
	WALArchiveDir	string
	// WALArchiveKey optionally encrypts archived WAL segments with a 32-byte
	// AES-256-GCM key when WALArchiveDir is set.
	WALArchiveKey	[]byte
	// TextSearchAnalyzers pre-registers custom Go text search analyzers keyed
	// by configuration name (ASCII case-folded to lowercase, 1..63 bytes,
	// without NUL bytes or dots). Invalid names, duplicate case-folded names,
	// or nil analyzers are rejected by Open with SQLSTATE 22023.
	TextSearchAnalyzers	map[string]TextSearchAnalyzer
}
```

Wait blocks until the next notification arrives, ctx is canceled, or the
subscription is closed.


### `type TextSearchAnalyzer`

TextSearchAnalyzer tokenizes and normalizes input text into lexemes for a
custom text search configuration (for example, a Korean/Japanese
morphological analyzer, n-gram tokenizer, or domain-specific stemmer).


```go
// TextSearchAnalyzer tokenizes and normalizes input text into lexemes for a
// custom text search configuration (for example, a Korean/Japanese
// morphological analyzer, n-gram tokenizer, or domain-specific stemmer).
type TextSearchAnalyzer func(ctx context.Context, input string) ([]TextSearchToken, error)
```

#### `func SimpleTextSearchAnalyzer(fn func(ctx context.Context, input string) ([]string, error)) TextSearchAnalyzer`

SimpleTextSearchAnalyzer adapts a tokenizer returning normalized lexeme
strings into a TextSearchAnalyzer with sequential 1-based positions and
default weight 'D'.


### `type TextSearchToken`

TextSearchToken is one normalized lexeme emitted by a user-registered
TextSearchAnalyzer.


```go
// TextSearchToken is one normalized lexeme emitted by a user-registered
// TextSearchAnalyzer.
type TextSearchToken struct {
	// Lexeme is the normalized token text. Empty lexemes are skipped.
	Lexeme	string
	// Position is the 1-based token position in the document (clamped to
	// PostgreSQL's 1..16383 range). A zero value auto-increments sequentially
	// from the previous token's position.
	Position	uint16
	// Weight is the optional PostgreSQL lexeme weight ('A', 'B', 'C', or 'D';
	// lowercase is accepted). Zero defaults to 'D'.
	Weight	byte
}
```

### `type UpgradeRequired`

UpgradeRequired reports a directory that holds a legacy database. Open never
writes to such a directory: the format is detected before any constructor runs
and the host must run the offline copy-upgrade instead.


```go
// UpgradeRequired reports a directory that holds a legacy database. Open never
// writes to such a directory: the format is detected before any constructor runs
// and the host must run the offline copy-upgrade instead.
type UpgradeRequired struct {
	Directory	string
	Cause		error
}
```

#### `func (e *UpgradeRequired) Error() string`

Error returns the upgrade-required message.


#### `func (e *UpgradeRequired) Unwrap() error`

Unwrap keeps the storage layer's own format verdict reachable.

## `pgx` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/pgx`.

### Package documentation

Package pgx provides a cleanroom, zero-external-dependency, in-process
pgx/v5-compatible API over supersql.


### Variables

#### `ErrNoRows, ErrTxClosed, ErrTxCommitRollback`

```go
var (
	// ErrNoRows occurs when rows are expected but none are returned.
	ErrNoRows	= sql.ErrNoRows

	// ErrTxClosed occurs when an operation is performed on a closed transaction.
	ErrTxClosed	= sql.ErrTxDone

	// ErrTxCommitRollback occurs when a commit fails and the transaction is rolled back.
	ErrTxCommitRollback	= errors.New("pgx: commit unexpectedly resulted in rollback")
)
```

### Functions

#### `func AppendRows[T any, S ~[]T](slice S, rows Rows, fn RowToFunc[T]) (S, error)`

AppendRows iterates through rows, calling fn for each row and appending the results to slice.


#### `func BeginFunc(ctx context.Context, db interface {
	Begin(ctx context.Context) (Tx, error)
}, fn func(Tx) error) (err error)`

BeginFunc begins a transaction on db and executes fn.


#### `func BeginTxFunc(ctx context.Context, db interface {
	BeginTx(ctx context.Context, txOptions TxOptions) (Tx, error)
}, txOptions TxOptions, fn func(Tx) error) (err error)`

BeginTxFunc begins a transaction with txOptions on db and executes fn.


#### `func CollectExactlyOneRow[T any](rows Rows, fn RowToFunc[T]) (T, error)`

CollectExactlyOneRow calls fn for the single row in rows and returns an error if 0 or >1 rows are returned.


#### `func CollectOneRow[T any](rows Rows, fn RowToFunc[T]) (T, error)`

CollectOneRow calls fn for the first row in rows and closes rows. Returns ErrNoRows if no rows are present.


#### `func CollectRows[T any](rows Rows, fn RowToFunc[T]) ([]T, error)`

CollectRows iterates through rows, calling fn for each row and collecting the results into a slice.


#### `func RowTo[T any](row CollectableRow) (T, error)`

RowTo scans a single column row into a value of type T.


#### `func RowToAddrOf[T any](row CollectableRow) (*T, error)`

RowToAddrOf scans a single column row into the address of a new value of type T.


#### `func RowToAddrOfStructByName[T any](row CollectableRow) (*T, error)`

RowToAddrOfStructByName returns a pointer to a struct of type T scanned by column name.


#### `func RowToAddrOfStructByNameLax[T any](row CollectableRow) (*T, error)`

RowToAddrOfStructByNameLax returns a pointer to a struct of type T scanned by column name (lax).


#### `func RowToAddrOfStructByPos[T any](row CollectableRow) (*T, error)`

RowToAddrOfStructByPos returns a pointer to a struct of type T scanned by field position.


#### `func RowToMap(row CollectableRow) (map[string]any, error)`

RowToMap scans a row into a map[string]any keyed by column name.


#### `func RowToStructByName[T any](row CollectableRow) (T, error)`

RowToStructByName scans a row into a struct of type T by matching column names to `db` tags or field names.


#### `func RowToStructByNameLax[T any](row CollectableRow) (T, error)`

RowToStructByNameLax scans a row into a struct of type T by name, ignoring extra columns or unmapped fields.


#### `func RowToStructByPos[T any](row CollectableRow) (T, error)`

RowToStructByPos scans a row into a struct of type T by field position.

## `pgwire` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/pgwire`.

### Package documentation

Package pgwire implements an optional, pure-Go (CGO_ENABLED=0) PostgreSQL
v3.0 wire protocol server over a SuperSQL Connector.

Each accepted TCP (or TLS-upgraded) client connection opens its own isolated
SQL session via Connector.Connect, keeping transactions, session settings,
prepared statements, portals, and temporary objects isolated per client.

Supported protocol capabilities include:
  - Startup negotiation: SSLRequest (TLS upgrade and enforcement when
    TLSConfig or RequireTLS is set), CancelRequest (unencrypted in-flight
    statement cancellation by PID/secret key), and StartupMessage v3.0.
  - Authentication: SCRAM-SHA-256 (AuthenticationSASL via PasswordLookup or
    Password), custom cleartext AuthFunc (AuthenticationCleartextPassword),
    or trust (AuthenticationOk).
  - Simple Query Protocol ('Q') with multi-statement splitting and accurate
    transaction status reporting ('I', 'T', 'E').
  - Extended Query Protocol ('P' Parse, 'B' Bind, 'D' Describe Statement and
    Portal, 'E' Execute with maxRows / PortalSuspended, 'C' Close, 'H' Flush,
    'S' Sync, 'X' Terminate) with text and binary parameter decoding,
    result encoding, and per-connection prepared statement / portal caps.
  - Asynchronous NotificationResponse ('A') delivery via Config.NotifyHandler,
    Server.Notify, or non-blocking Server.BroadcastNotify with bounded write
    deadlines for LISTEN/NOTIFY integration.


### Types

#### `type Config`

Config configures a PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol Server.


```go
// Config configures a PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol Server.
type Config struct {
	// Connector supplies isolated SuperSQL sessions per client connection.
	// If passed to NewServer directly, that argument takes precedence.
	Connector	*supersql.Connector

	// Password enables SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication when non-empty and both
	// PasswordLookup and AuthFunc are nil. It may be either a plaintext
	// password or a PostgreSQL SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier string. When Password,
	// PasswordLookup, and AuthFunc are all empty/nil, trust authentication
	// (AuthenticationOk) is used.
	Password	string

	// PasswordLookup looks up the expected credential for (user, database)
	// during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. It may return either a plaintext
	// password or a PostgreSQL SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier string in the format
	// "SCRAM-SHA-256$<iterations>:<b64salt>$<b64storedKey>:<b64serverKey>".
	// When non-nil, PasswordLookup takes precedence over AuthFunc and Password.
	PasswordLookup	func(ctx context.Context, user, database string) (string, error)

	// AuthFunc optionally overrides password verification with custom cleartext
	// password logic when PasswordLookup is nil. Returning a non-nil error
	// rejects the client with SQLSTATE 28P01 (or the error's SQLSTATE if it
	// carries one).
	AuthFunc	func(ctx context.Context, user, database, password string) error

	// TLSConfig enables SSLRequest ('S') upgrades via tls.Server and requires
	// TLS for StartupMessage connections when non-nil. When nil (and RequireTLS
	// is false), SSLRequest is declined with 'N'.
	TLSConfig	*tls.Config

	// RequireTLS rejects clients that do not upgrade to TLS via SSLRequest.
	// NewServer returns an error if RequireTLS is true and TLSConfig is nil.
	RequireTLS	bool

	// MaxConnections caps concurrent active authenticated client sessions.
	// Defaults to 128.
	MaxConnections	int

	// MaxPreAuthPerIP caps concurrent unauthenticated (pre-auth) connections
	// allowed from a single remote IP address. Defaults to 32 (capped at the
	// global pre-auth limit) when zero or negative.
	MaxPreAuthPerIP	int

	// MaxPreparedStatements caps the number of prepared statements cached per
	// connection. Defaults to 1024 when zero or negative.
	MaxPreparedStatements	int

	// MaxPortals caps the number of open portals per connection. Defaults to
	// 256 when zero or negative.
	MaxPortals	int

	// ReadTimeout bounds individual wire frame reads, startup negotiation, and
	// TLS handshakes. Defaults to 30s when zero; set a negative duration to
	// disable read timeouts.
	ReadTimeout	time.Duration

	// WriteTimeout bounds socket write and flush operations. Defaults to 30s
	// when zero; set a negative duration to disable write timeouts.
	WriteTimeout	time.Duration

	// IdleTimeout bounds how long an idle connection may wait for the next
	// frontend message before being closed. Defaults to 5m when zero; set a
	// negative duration to disable idle timeouts.
	IdleTimeout	time.Duration

	// ApplicationVersion is reported in the server_version ParameterStatus.
	// Defaults to "18.4 (SuperSQL)".
	ApplicationVersion	string

	// Logger receives optional diagnostic log lines.
	Logger	func(format string, args ...any)

	// NotifyHandler is invoked once per authenticated connection with the
	// connection's context, backend PID, and a thread-safe NotifySender that
	// pushes NotificationResponse ('A') frames over the wire. The optional
	// returned cleanup function is called when the connection closes.
	NotifyHandler	func(ctx context.Context, pid int32, send NotifySender) (cleanup func())
}
```

#### `type Notification`

Notification represents an asynchronous PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY payload
delivered over the wire as a NotificationResponse ('A') frame.


```go
// Notification represents an asynchronous PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY payload
// delivered over the wire as a NotificationResponse ('A') frame.
type Notification struct {
	PID	int32
	Channel	string
	Payload	string
}
```

#### `type NotifySender`

NotifySender delivers asynchronous NotificationResponse ('A') frames to a
connected client. It is safe for concurrent use from any goroutine.


```go
// NotifySender delivers asynchronous NotificationResponse ('A') frames to a
// connected client. It is safe for concurrent use from any goroutine.
type NotifySender func(Notification) error
```

#### `type Server`

Server accepts PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol connections and routes each
client to its own isolated SuperSQL session.


```go
// Server accepts PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol connections and routes each
// client to its own isolated SuperSQL session.
type Server struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

##### `func NewServer(connector *supersql.Connector, cfg Config) (*Server, error)`

NewServer constructs a PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol Server over connector.
The server borrows connector and never closes it when Server.Close is called.


##### `func NewServerFromCatalog(db *supersql.Catalog, cfg Config) (*Server, error)`

NewServerFromCatalog is a convenience constructor wrapping an already opened
*supersql.Catalog. Closing the returned Server does not close db.


##### `func (s *Server) ActiveConnections() int`

ActiveConnections reports the number of currently active authenticated client
sessions.


##### `func (s *Server) Addr() net.Addr`

Addr returns the listener's network address once Serve or ListenAndServe has
bound a listener, or nil before serving starts.


##### `func (s *Server) BroadcastNotify(senderPID int32, channel, payload string)`

BroadcastNotify enqueues an asynchronous NotificationResponse ('A') frame to
every currently connected client without blocking on slow or stalled peers.


##### `func (s *Server) Close() error`

Close stops accepting new connections, closes all active client connections,
and waits for all connection goroutines to finish. It does not close the
underlying *supersql.Connector.


##### `func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(ctx context.Context, addr string) error`

ListenAndServe listens on TCP address addr (e.g. "127.0.0.1:5432" or
"127.0.0.1:0") and serves PostgreSQL v3.0 wire protocol clients until ctx is
canceled or Close is called.


##### `func (s *Server) Notify(pid int32, channel, payload string) error`

Notify delivers an asynchronous NotificationResponse ('A') frame to the
client connection identified by pid.


##### `func (s *Server) Serve(ctx context.Context, ln net.Listener) error`

Serve accepts incoming connections on ln and serves them until ctx is
canceled, Close is called, or ln returns a fatal error.


## `clock` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/clock`.

### Package documentation

Package clock defines certified continuous SI time independently of a provider.


### Constants

#### `ScaleName`

ScaleName is the canonical identifier for the continuous SI nanosecond scale.


```go
// ScaleName is the canonical identifier for the continuous SI nanosecond scale.
const ScaleName = "si_ns_1970"
```

### Variables

#### `ErrClockUnavailable, ErrClockEpochChanged, ErrClockRange`

Sentinel errors returned by certified Clock implementations.


```go
// Sentinel errors returned by certified Clock implementations.
var (
	ErrClockUnavailable	= errors.New("certified clock unavailable")
	ErrClockEpochChanged	= errors.New("certified clock epoch changed")
	ErrClockRange		= errors.New("certified clock value out of range")
)
```

#### `ErrClockScale`

ErrClockScale reports an invalid or incompatible SI scale descriptor or leap-second history.


```go
// ErrClockScale reports an invalid or incompatible SI scale descriptor or leap-second history.
var ErrClockScale = errors.New("incompatible SI clock scale or leap history")
```

### Functions

#### `func ValidateScale(ctx context.Context, scale ScaleDescriptor, maxBytes uint64) error`

ValidateScale validates the provider-independent GSTL1 persistence contract.
It borrows the descriptor only through this call and allocates no entry table.


#### `func ValidateScaleExtension(ctx context.Context, previous, next ScaleDescriptor, protected Instant, maxBytes uint64) error`

ValidateScaleExtension permits only an unchanged history or appended entries
whose first affected SI instant is strictly beyond the protected timestamp.


### Types

#### `type Clock`

Clock is borrowed by the database; its host owns provider startup and shutdown.
Reads and waits must be concurrency-safe and honor cancellation without
per-request network polling. Failed assurance must never return an estimate.


```go
// Clock is borrowed by the database; its host owns provider startup and shutdown.
// Reads and waits must be concurrency-safe and honor cancellation without
// per-request network polling. Failed assurance must never return an estimate.
type Clock interface {
	// Read returns a fresh nonnegative closed interval in Synced or Holdover
	// status, validated against the provider's width, raw age and continuity bounds.
	Read(context.Context) (Reading, error)
	// WaitUntilAfter requires a fresh valid sample in exactly epoch proving
	// Earliest > target. Equality, elapsed timers and stale watermarks do not suffice.
	WaitUntilAfter(context.Context, Instant, Epoch) error
	// Scale returns owned canonical GSTL1 bytes; mutating them cannot alter the provider.
	Scale() ScaleDescriptor
	FromUTC(time.Time) (Instant, error)
	ToUTC(Instant) (UTCProjection, error)
}
```

#### `type Epoch`

Epoch identifies a continuous certified-clock assurance epoch, leap-second
history, and provider configuration.


```go
// Epoch identifies a continuous certified-clock assurance epoch, leap-second
// history, and provider configuration.
type Epoch struct {
	Assurance	[16]byte
	LeapHistory	[32]byte
	Config		[32]byte
}
```

#### `type Instant`

Instant counts SI nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC, including leap seconds.


```go

```

#### `type Reading`

Reading is a certified closed SI interval [Earliest, Latest] with its epoch
and synchronization status.


```go

// and synchronization status.

```

#### `type ScaleDescriptor`

ScaleDescriptor carries the SI scale name and canonical GSTL1 leap-second

```go
// history bytes with their SHA-256 identity.

```

Status reports the synchronization state of a certified clock reading.


```go

```

UTCProjection is the civil UTC projection of an SI Instant, with LeapSecond

## `clock/local` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/clock/local` (package `localclock`).

### Package documentation

Package localclock provides a standalone single-process clock.Clock backed by
the host OS wall and monotonic clocks. It requires no external NTP or PTP
synchronization and is intended for single-process embedded databases.


### Types

#### `type Clock`

Clock is a concurrency-safe standalone clock.Clock backed by the host OS wall
and monotonic clocks with a strict monotonic high-water mark.


```go
// Clock is a concurrency-safe standalone clock.Clock backed by the host OS wall
// and monotonic clocks with a strict monotonic high-water mark.
type Clock struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

##### `func New(opts ...Option) *Clock`

New constructs a standalone local clock with safe zero-config defaults.


##### `func (c *Clock) FromUTC(value time.Time) (clock.Instant, error)`

FromUTC converts a UTC timestamp to its SI nanosecond instant under this
clock's canonical GSTL1 leap history.


##### `func (c *Clock) Read(ctx context.Context) (clock.Reading, error)`

Read returns a fresh nonnegative closed interval [Earliest, Latest] in
clock.Synced status. Readings never move backward even if the OS wall clock
steps backward.


##### `func (c *Clock) Scale() clock.ScaleDescriptor`

Scale returns owned canonical GSTL1 bytes; mutating them cannot alter the clock.


##### `func (c *Clock) ToUTC(value clock.Instant) (clock.UTCProjection, error)`

ToUTC projects an SI nanosecond instant onto UTC under this clock's canonical
GSTL1 leap history. An inserted positive leap second projects onto the
preceding UTC second with LeapSecond set.


##### `func (c *Clock) WaitUntilAfter(ctx context.Context, target clock.Instant, epoch clock.Epoch) error`

WaitUntilAfter blocks until a fresh reading in epoch proves Earliest > target,
or until ctx is canceled.


#### `type Option`

Option configures a local Clock constructed by New.


```go
// Option configures a local Clock constructed by New.
type Option func(*config)
```

##### `func WithInitialFloor(floor clock.Instant) Option`

WithInitialFloor sets a minimum starting SI instant for the clock.
Negative values are clamped to zero.


##### `func WithUncertainty(d time.Duration) Option`

WithUncertainty configures the interval width (Latest - Earliest) returned by
Read. Negative values are clamped to zero. The default is zero.


## `clock/gstime` package reference

Import path `github.com/gosuda/supersql-alpha/clock/gstime` (package `gstimeclock`).

### Package documentation

Package gstimeclock adapts gstime's certified SI intervals; it does not qualify raw backends.


### Functions

#### `func New(service *gstime.ClockService, history *gstime.LeapHistory) (clock.Clock, error)`

New borrows a service, which may still be unanchored. Its caller owns workers,
raw-clock qualification and invalidation, and must keep the service history immutable.


### Types

#### `type Config`

Config configures a gstime-backed certified clock Provider.


```go
// Config configures a gstime-backed certified clock Provider.
type Config struct {
	Sync	config.Config
	// Raw must include suspend; its physical bounds and sources remain caller-qualified.
	Raw		rawclock.RawClock
	LeapHistory	*gstime.LeapHistory
}
```

#### `type Provider`

Provider owns its synchronization worker until Close cancels and joins it.
Open's context bounds initialization; the supplied raw clock remains caller-owned.


```go
// Provider owns its synchronization worker until Close cancels and joins it.
// Open's context bounds initialization; the supplied raw clock remains caller-owned.
type Provider struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

##### `func Open(ctx context.Context, cfg Config) (*Provider, error)`

Open starts a gstime synchronization engine, waits for initial sync within
ctx, and returns a certified clock Provider.


##### `func (p *Provider) Close() error`

Close cancels the synchronization worker and closes the underlying gstime
engine. It is safe to call more than once.


##### `func (c Provider) FromUTC(value time.Time) (clock.Instant, error)`

FromUTC converts a civil UTC timestamp into a continuous SI Instant using
the clock's leap-second history.


##### `func (c Provider) Read(ctx context.Context) (clock.Reading, error)`

Read returns a validated certified SI interval from the underlying gstime service.


##### `func (c Provider) Scale() clock.ScaleDescriptor`

Scale returns an owned copy of the canonical GSTL1 scale descriptor.


##### `func (c Provider) ToUTC(instant clock.Instant) (clock.UTCProjection, error)`

ToUTC projects a continuous SI Instant onto a civil UTC timestamp and
reports whether the instant lies inside a positive leap second.


##### `func (c Provider) WaitUntilAfter(ctx context.Context, target clock.Instant, epoch clock.Epoch) error`

WaitUntilAfter blocks until a fresh certified reading in epoch proves
Earliest > target, or until ctx or the provider lifetime ends.
